root_cause.text: The driver was passing stack-allocated buffers to spi_read(), which violates DMA safety requirements because stack memory may not be DMA-coherent and can cause cache coherency issues or memory corruption when used with DMA operations.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces stack-allocated local variables (`__be16 buf` and `__be32 buf`) with a DMA-safe buffer (`u8 buf[3] __aligned(IIO_DMA_MINALIGN)`) allocated as part of the device data structure. The commit message explicitly states "All SPI buffers must be DMA-safe" and the fix adds proper alignment using `IIO_DMA_MINALIGN` to ensure the buffer meets DMA coherency requirements. The original code at lines 83-84 and 90-91 passed the address of stack variables directly to `spi_read()`, which is unsafe for DMA operations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add unaligned memory access header to support safe unaligned data operations in the driver.
intent_record.what: Added `#include <linux/unaligned.h>` header file after the existing `#include <linux/spi/spi.h>` line in the include section.
intent_record.how: This inclusion makes unaligned memory access macros and functions available to the compilation unit, enabling the code to safely read from or write to unaligned memory addresses without triggering alignment faults on strict-alignment architectures.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a DMA-safe aligned buffer to the ti_adc_data structure to prevent DMA coherency issues during ADC measurements.
intent_record.what: Added a new field `u8 buf[3] __aligned(IIO_DMA_MINALIGN);` to the `ti_adc_data` structure after the `shift` field.
intent_record.how: This change allocates a 3-byte buffer within the device data structure with DMA-safe alignment guarantees. The `__aligned(IIO_DMA_MINALIGN)` attribute ensures the buffer meets the minimum alignment requirements for DMA operations, preventing potential DMA coherency issues and cache line conflicts that could occur with unaligned buffers.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace unsafe stack-allocated buffers with a shared DMA-safe buffer and use proper unaligned access helpers to prevent memory corruption from unaligned SPI reads.
intent_record.what: Removed local stack-allocated buffers (buf) from case 2 and case 3 blocks and replaced them with a shared data->buf pointer. Changed endianness conversion from be16_to_cpu(buf) to get_unaligned_be16(data->buf) for case 2, and from be32_to_cpu(buf) >> 8 to get_unaligned_be24(data->buf) for case 3. Removed the explicit block scope braces around each case.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates stack allocation overhead by reusing a pre-allocated buffer in the data structure. The get_unaligned_be* functions handle both endianness conversion and unaligned memory access atomically, replacing the previous pattern of casting a stack pointer and manually shifting bits. This prevents potential stack corruption from unaligned SPI reads and improves memory safety by using a dedicated DMA-safe buffer.

The group directly addresses the vulnerability root cause by replacing stack-allocated buffers with DMA-safe aligned buffers and using proper unaligned access helpers. This eliminates the DMA coherency issues and memory corruption risks that occur when stack memory is passed to DMA operations like spi_read().

Author: Matt Ranostay <mranostay@gmail.com>
Date:   Fri Aug 19 20:17:03 2016 -0700

    iio: adc: ti-adc161s626: add support for TI 1-channel differential ADCs
    
    Add support for Texas Instruments ADC141S626, and ADC161S626 chips.
    
    Signed-off-by: Matt Ranostay <mranostay@gmail.com>
    Signed-off-by: Jonathan Cameron <jic23@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/iio/adc/ti-adc161s626.c b/drivers/iio/adc/ti-adc161s626.c
new file mode 100644
bic_trace_step.reason: The function `ti_adc_read_measurement()` contains the vulnerable construct. At lines 81-87 and 89-95, stack-allocated buffers (`__be16 buf` and `__be32 buf`) are passed directly to `spi_read(data->spi, (void *) &buf, ...)`. These are local variables on the stack, which violates DMA safety requirements because stack memory is not guaranteed to be DMA-coherent. The struct `ti_adc_data` does define a properly aligned buffer at line 72 (`u8 buffer[16] ____cacheline_aligned;`), but this is not used in `ti_adc_read_measurement()`. Instead, the function uses temporary stack-allocated buffers for the SPI read operations, which can cause cache coherency issues or memory corruption when used with DMA. The fix is not present in this commit - the code should use the pre-allocated `data->buffer` member instead of stack variables.
